Compute modules relationship

compute.modules.relationship.Rd

Correlates every column of one matrix with every column of another (e.g., TF modules and external features such as deconvolution estimates or pathway activities) across the same set of samples, and visualizes the significant associations. It is meant for continuous variables only: all the columns of both matrices must be numeric. For categorical variables (e.g. clinical groups), use compute.metadata.association().

Usage

compute.modules.relationship(
  matA,
  matB,
  file_name = NULL,
  batch = NULL,
  pval = 0.05,
  padj = FALSE,
  cor_type = "p",
  vertical = F,
  plot = T,
  plot.grid = F,
  ncol.grid = NULL
)

Arguments

matA

A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features (samples x features), e.g. TF module scores.

matB

A numeric matrix or data frame of continuous features to correlate with (samples x features).

file_name

A string indicating the base name (without extension) of the figures to be saved in the "Results/" folder. If NULL (default), no figure is saved.

batch

Optional vector indicating batch assignment for samples (no missing values). If it has two or more levels, partial correlations (ppcor::pcor.test(), Pearson or Spearman according to cor_type) are computed controlling for batch. Batch is treated as categorical (one dummy variable per level beyond the first).

pval

A numeric threshold for the p-value to define significance (p-value, or adjusted p-value with padj = TRUE, <= pval). Default is 0.05.

padj

Logical; if TRUE, the p-values are corrected for multiple testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg method, across the columns of matB for each column of matA, and the adjusted p-values are used to define significance (in significant and in the figures). Default is FALSE.

cor_type

Type of correlation to compute: "p" (Pearson) or "s" (Spearman). Default is "p". It also sets the type of the partial correlations computed with batch.

vertical

Logical; if TRUE, modules are on the x-axis and the matB features on the y-axis. Otherwise (default), the matB features are on the x-axis and modules on the y-axis.

plot

Logical; if TRUE, saves the heatmap plot as a PDF (file_name is needed). Default is TRUE.

plot.grid

Logical; if TRUE, generates per-pair scatter grid plots for significant associations, saved to "Results/<file_name>_scatter_grid.svg" (the 100 strongest pairs at most). With Spearman, the ranks of the values are shown, as the correlation is computed on them. With batch, the values shown are corrected for batch, as the correlations are. Default is FALSE.

ncol.grid

Integer number of columns used in scatter grid layout. If NULL (default), it is set to the ceiling of the square root of the number of panels.

Value

Invisibly, a list with:

  • correlation: the correlation matrix (columns of matA as rows, columns of matB as columns).

  • significant: a named list with, for each column of matA, the columns of matB significantly correlated with it (p-value, or adjusted p-value with padj = TRUE, <= pval).

  • p_value: the matrix of p-values.

  • p_adjusted: the matrix of Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values (equal to p_value with padj = FALSE).

If plot = TRUE and file_name is given, a heatmap of the correlations is saved to "Results/<file_name>.pdf" (the ".pdf" extension is added if missing). Its size is computed from the number of features. With up to 40 features per axis, the significant cells show the correlation and its significance (* < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001, **** < 0.0001); with more, they are marked with an asterisk.

Details

matA and matB must have the same samples in the same order (same rownames); names are compared after make.names(), so e.g. "TCGA-XX" and "TCGA.XX" match. Correlations and p-values use, for each pair of columns, the samples with a value in both (missing values are allowed); a pair with fewer than three such samples, or without variation among them, gets NA. Columns without variation are skipped with a message. Column names must be unique within each matrix.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
corr = compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]],
                                    deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]],
                                    plot = FALSE,
                                    pval = 0.01)
corr$correlation[1:3, 1:3]
